threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look at the bus stop timetable like it means something, instead of just setting your watch to 'eventually'.
Caught the 196 last night, and there was a guy reciting Shakespeare to a bemused crowd. Only in Brixton, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The way the kebab shop owner knows your order without you saying a word. That's when it hit me—it's more than just a place, it's home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg will you find a kebab shop that proudly displays its 'Best Currywurst' award in the window—right next to the doner meat. It’s a delicious identity crisis.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know a true local when they can navigate the BART delays and still manage to make it to La Taqueria for a burrito, no matter what.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: I watched a guy serenade the bus with a ukulele today; his best audience was a couple of pigeons perched on the stop sign.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all the local bars serve only tapas, but the best are the unmarked ones that just do vermut on tap, no frills.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You’ll notice them standing at every crosswalk, waiting for the light to change even when no cars are in sight.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You call it a ‘flat’ instead of an 'apartment' and wonder why everyone looks at you funny when you mention taking the Tube to get to Shoreditch.
Caught the 35 last night; some bloke was trying to barter with the driver for a free ride, claiming he had 'good vibes' instead of cash. Driver just laughed.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When you see a group of kids practicing breakdancing on the sidewalk while the kebab shop serves up at 3am. That's Neukölln in a nutshell.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find 24-hour Turkish döner stands where locals debate the best sauce at 3 AM. The energy is unmatched.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they order a burrito without guac and still give the cashier a nod like it’s a secret pact.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy juggling on the bus today while a woman was ranting about her lost cat. Only in SF do you get street performers and real-life drama on the Muni.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Most tourists think Gràcia is just about Gaudí, but the true magic lies in the tiny plazas where locals sip vermut and ignore the rush.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a newbie by the way they still try to order a 'café con leche' in the smallest bars, where it's just 'café' or 'cortado' that gets you anywhere.
